title: Anti-fraud overhaul clears House despite Democratic concerns over privacy and IG independence
summary: Many Democrats opposed the measure due to fears the Trump administration would exert more political influence on inspectors general as well as concerns about privacy risk.

title: Senate rejects Cyber Force push as debate over cyber structure continues
summary: Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand’s amendment to place a new service under the Army fell short in committee, even as lawmakers advanced separate provisions examining Cyber Command’s role and resourcing.

title: Lawmakers press for tighter oversight of fast-growing prediction markets
summary: Senators are urging the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to clarify rules for event contracts and strengthen monitoring standards, warning that rapid growth in prediction markets is exposing weaknesses in safeguards against manipulation and consumer harm.

title: Surveillance authority nears historic lapse as House deadlock meets intelligence leadership fight
summary: Section 702 is set to expire for the first time after a failed House vote, even as a White House nomination aims to resolve a separate battle over who should oversee the intelligence community during the transition.

title: Expanding paid leave for federal workers is back on the table
summary: Bipartisan legislation would grant civilian federal employees up to 12 weeks of paid family and medical leave per year.

title: Most Americans think government workers are competent and should be nonpartisan, according to recent surveys
summary: A survey from the Partnership for Public Service also found that a majority of Americans oppose the Trump administration’s changes to government.

title: Why Social Security’s funding gap matters to federal retirement
summary: Most federal employees under FERS rely on Social Security as part of retirement. The latest trustees report suggests the choices to preserve full benefits are getting tougher.

title: DOJ shutters alleged China-linked operation targeting current and former feds
summary: The sites posed as consulting companies and used paid research opportunities to connect with people holding national security expertise, prosecutors said.

title: Return-to-office push put GSA’s network infrastructure to the test
summary: A recent upgrade project offers a glimpse at how one agency adapted its technology footprint as more federal employees returned to government offices.

title: Bisignano deflects customer service questions in congressional testimony
summary: The Social Security commissioner frequently tried to shout over Democratic lawmakers during the occasionally raucous hearing.

title: A year after sounding the alarm, NIH dissenters say political influence is entrenched at research agency
summary: The Trump administration has cut staff and grants at the National Institutes of Health, and employees warn further overhauls appear to be likely.

title: OPM's long-planned HR overhaul moves ahead with $396M award to Oracle
summary: The agency plans to consolidate more than 100 personnel systems into a single platform serving 2 million federal employees.

title: Why Congress separated immigration funding from oversight
summary: After negotiations over enforcement restrictions collapsed, lawmakers approved $70 billion, funding that will give the Trump administration resources to continue its immigration crackdown through nearly the end of the president's second term.

title: Building cyber-resilient payroll systems in government
summary: COMMENTARY | Cybersecurity needs to be built into everything that keeps government running, especially as payroll is one of the most critical systems in operation.

title: NDA proposal for feds draws scrutiny on Capitol Hill
summary: Rep. Raja Krishnamoorth, D-Ill., expressed “serious concern” about the Office of Personnel Management’s controversial proposal,  including its impact on whistleblowers and employees who report wrongdoing.

title: After year of pushing employees out, OPM embraces familiar recruiting playbook
summary: In order for agencies to attain top talent, Office of Personnel Director Scott Kupor pointed to job websites specific to college students, multi-agency position postings and tech recruiting programs — all strategies that the Biden administration also employed.

title: GAO warns detention camp failures could become a blueprint for billions in new spending
summary: The watchdog found contracting missteps, health lapses and oversight breakdowns at a Texas immigration facility, raising concerns as the federal government moves ahead with a far larger detention expansion.

title: Union renews call for lawmakers to override Trump’s anti-union EO at the Pentagon
summary: Last year, the House voted to pass its annual defense policy bill with a provision that would have halted implementation of President Trump’s executive order banning collective bargaining at the Defense Department and other agencies, but the Senate axed the measure.

title: Practical steps agencies can take to mitigate financial disclosure controversies
summary: COMMENTARY | Decentralized handling of supplemental forms like travel reimbursements and widely attended gatherings can create ethical blind spots that bad actors can exploit.

title: Another lawsuit alleges DOJ is illegally rejecting telework requests from employees with disabilities
summary: Some of the plaintiffs said that the revocations of their telework reasonable accommodations have forced them to take leave and worsened their health.

title: What makes an effective intelligence chief? A former DNI official points to the answer
summary: COMMENTARY | As scrutiny grows around President Trump’s pick to lead the intelligence community, a former National Intelligence Council chair explains the less visible responsibilities that come with the job.

title: VA CIO nominee vows to create program management office
summary: Gary Shatswell, President Donald Trump’s pick to helm VA’s IT operations, told lawmakers creating the office is “one of the first tasks that I will be going after” if confirmed to the role.

title: Trump memo pushes national security agencies to move faster on AI
summary: The directive calls for deeper partnerships with AI companies while directing agencies to guard frontier models and the data centers that power them from foreign adversaries.

title: Lawmakers aim to force the Army to detail its transformation plans
summary: “Parochial interests” may have motivated lawmakers to tighten the reins, one official said.

title: Trump’s edict making 8,000 feds at-will employees draws swift outcry
summary: Agencies have just one week to reclassify thousands of federal workers in purportedly policy-related roles into the new Schedule Policy/Career, stripping them of most civil service protections.
